facts: $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=x(t)\underset{\sim}{i}+y(t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ says the particle is $x(t)$ across and $y(t)$ up at time $t$.
To find the position at a particular time, substitute that value of $t$ into both components.
The pair $x=x(t)$ and $y=y(t)$ are **parametric equations** for the path, with time as the parameter.
The particle's distance from the origin at time $t$ is $\sqrt{x(t)^{2}+y(t)^{2}}$.
The **path** is the curve the particle traces out, and it does not show when the particle reaches each point.
The particle is on the $y$-axis when $x(t)=0$, and on the $x$-axis when $y(t)=0$.
Time is usually restricted to $t\ge0$, so only part of the curve is traced.
steps: Write down the two component functions $x(t)$ and $y(t)$.
Substitute the given value of $t$ into each component.
State the position as a vector or as a point.

foundation.question_text: A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(3t+1)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t-5)\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find its position when $t=4$.
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{2}-2t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(5-t)\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find its position when $t=3$.
A particle starts at the point $(2,-3)$. After $t$ seconds it has moved $4t$ units to the right and $3t$ units up from its starting point. Write its position vector function $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$.
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t+1)\underset{\sim}{i}+2t\underset{\sim}{j}$. How far is the particle from the origin when $t=2$?
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t-6)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}+1)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge0$. At what time is the particle on the $y$-axis?
A particle is at $(-1,7)$ when $t=0$. Its $x$-coordinate decreases by $2$ each second and its $y$-coordinate never changes. Write its position vector function $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$.
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=4\underset{\sim}{i}+(t-2)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge0$. Describe the motion of the particle.
foundation.solution_text:
$x(t)=4$ for every value of $t$, so the particle stays on the vertical line $x=4$.
$y(t)=t-2$ increases by $1$ each second, starting at $y=-2$.
The particle moves straight up the line $x=4$, starting at $(4,-2)$ and rising $1$ unit each second.

development.question_text: A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=6\cos t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+6\sin t\,\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find its exact position when $t=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$.
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{2}-9)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t+1)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge0$. Find the position of the particle when it crosses the $y$-axis.
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(3t-1)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t+3)\underset{\sim}{j}$. How far is the particle from the origin when $t=3$?
At time $t$ a particle's $x$-coordinate is three less than twice $t$, and its $y$-coordinate is the square of $t$. Write its position vector function $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$.
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(2+t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(6-t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge0$. Describe the motion of the particle.
development.solution_text:
$x(t)=2+t$ increases by $1$ each second, starting at $x=2$.
$y(t)=6-t$ decreases by $1$ each second, starting at $y=6$.
The particle moves in a straight line from $(2,6)$, going $1$ unit right and $1$ unit down each second.

development.question_text: A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{3}-4t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}+t)\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find its position when $t=2$.
A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(2t+3)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-4t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge0$. Find all times at which the particle is on the $x$-axis.
development.solution_text:
On the $x$-axis the $y$-component is zero.
$t^{2}-4t=0$
$t(t-4)=0$
$t=0$ or $t=4$

mastery.question_text: A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t-5)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t+1)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge0$. Find the time at which the particle is closest to the origin, and its exact distance from the origin then.
A particle moves in a straight line at a steady rate. It is at $(2,5)$ when $t=0$ and at $(14,-3)$ when $t=4$. Write its position vector function $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$.
mastery.solution_text:
Change in position over $4$ seconds $=(14-2)\underset{\sim}{i}+(-3-5)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=12\underset{\sim}{i}-8\underset{\sim}{j}$
Change each second $=3\underset{\sim}{i}-2\underset{\sim}{j}$
$\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(2+3t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(5-2t)\underset{\sim}{j}$

mastery.question_text: A particle has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(t^{2}-2t-3)\underset{\sim}{i}+(t^{2}-9)\underset{\sim}{j}$ for $t\ge0$. Show that the particle passes through the origin and find the time at which it does so.
mastery.solution_text:
At the origin both components are zero.
$t^{2}-2t-3=0$
$(t-3)(t+1)=0$
$t=3$ (since $t\ge0$)
$t^{2}-9=0$
$t=3$ (since $t\ge0$)
Both components are zero at $t=3$, so the particle passes through the origin when $t=3$.
